creator: Alexander Terp
description:
From #153, batch 9, item 1, and batch 11, item 5.

A script has no built-in way to find its own file, and the closest workaround does not resolve symlinks. `get_path(get_args()[0]).full_path` returns the link's path:

```
repo/bin/tool.rad
link-dir/tool.rad -> ../repo/bin/tool.rad

$ rad link-dir/tool.rad
full_path: .../link-dir/tool.rad   type: file
```

Batch 9: an installer symlinked a CLI into `~/.local/bin`, so every repo-relative path (data dir, archive, test fixtures) resolved under `~/.local`. `report` printed "No data", `selftest` found no fixtures and `doctor` stayed green. Silent wrong behavior; the fix was `quiet $`readlink -f ...`` at startup. `get_path` exposes no link target, and `rad docs get_path` describes `full_path` as "Absolute path", which reads as resolved.

Batch 11: a tool installed by Homebrew or from a clone wanted a `skill` command printing a file kept next to the script, and ended up embedding the 200-line file as a raw string.

The stdlib-gaps card (a_25NhzP3KK) lists `script_path()`/`script_dir()` and symlink info in `get_path`, backed by a third script (`msh:227-229`, which shells `dirname "$(realpath ...)"`).

Wanted: `script_path()` (resolved) or a `real_path()` builtin plus a link field on `get_path`. At minimum, `rad docs get_path` should say `full_path` does not resolve symlinks.

Confirmed on main (3459ddf1).

Where: docs/funcs/get_path.md, new docs/funcs/*.md builtin, core/funcs.go.
title: Let a script find its own path, resolving symlinks
